text:
Alex: Deploy-bot flagged a release during the change window, need quick decision on semver.
deploy-bot: auto-release requested for package "inference-core" from 1.12.3 -> suggested bump: 1.12.4 (patch) based on changelog tags. Trigger: scheduled surge window.
Priya: Patch seems fine, but the change touches feature flags — does that count as behavior change? :thinking_face: 
Jordan: It's a config toggle default change. No API changes. I'd treat as patch unless it alters external contract.
Sam: Worth confirming tests. Failing e2e on canary last night but flaked. Do we have a rollback plan if it regresses? :roll_eyes: 
Maya: Rollback plan: new release can be reverted by `git tag -d` and deploybot rollback at route-level, + traffic shift back to previous variant. Ops playbook link: https://wikilink/rollbacks
Priya: Tagging conventions — should we include buildmeta? Our last naming used `v1.12.4+build.2026-03-15`. That caused pinning surprises for downstream consumers.
Alex: My vote: prefer simple `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tags in repo, and add buildmeta in CI artifact names only. Keeps semver comparisons clean.
Jordan: Agreed. Also let's avoid prerelease suffixes for hotfixes during change window unless truly gated.
Sam: For this case, I'm leaning patch. But let's add an explicit release note line: "Toggle default to X guarded by feature flag; no external API change; rollback via route pinning." Minimal but useful.
Priya: Can we also annotate the deploybot message with `changelog: patch` or `bump:patch` so automated tooling can pick it up?
deploy-bot: acknowledged. Will add metadata field `bump: patch` and `change_window: surge-3h` to the release payload.
Maya: One more ask — if we tag patch, downstream packages that pin `~1.12.3` will pick this up. Is that intended? Some infra services pin to `^` or `~` inconsistently.
Alex: Good catch. If we think consumers shouldn't pick this up automatically, we should publish a note and consider a minor bump. But that seems heavy for a toggle.
Jordan: Practically, most internal services pin exact versions in manifests. External libs might be more liberal. Given low risk, patch is ok. We'll monitor telemetry for 2 hours post-deploy.
Sam: Who's owning the post-deploy watch? I'll take first 30m then handoff to oncall.
Priya: I'll write the single-line release note and approve the tag. `git tag -a v1.12.4 -m "patch: feature flag default change (safe rollback)"`
Alex: :thumbsup: Priya please push and trigger deploybot.
Priya: done. `git push origin refs/tags/v1.12.4`
deploy-bot: deploy started to surge window (region: us-east1), canary 5% -> 20% over 20m. Monitoring hooks enabled.
Sam: Watching logs, will post updates. If errors > 0.5% for 5m I'll flip rollback.
Maya: Documenting this under release-notes: "v1.12.4 — patch: toggle default for X behind feature flag. Rollback: tag revert + deploybot route pin." Link to note: https://wikilink/releases/1.12.4
Jordan: Postmortem requirements: only if we hit rollback. Otherwise just annotate changelog and close.
Alex: Thanks team. Keeping the tag simple and deploy metadata explicit seems like the right balance. :white_check_mark:
Sam: 10m into canary — no uptick yet.
Priya: 25m — moving to 50%.
Maya: Telemetry stable. I'll update the release note with metrics snapshot after 2h.
Priya: final: pushed changelog entry and release note. Closing thread unless rollback triggered.
